prBody:
Go dependency fan-out over 300 extra cases now runs the full gate. Browser source selection requires complete per-spec V8 observations for the exact base tree, merged with imports; missing, stale, partial, new/renamed, CSS, asset and data inputs use the full browser layout. D3 remains A (CI_AFFECTED_LANE is unchanged).

Baseline: Arion v5 W2 (2026-10-05 00:00–2026-10-09 04:00 UTC): first-attempt green 62.3% (266/427), required-check green 65.8%, PR CI p50 16.1 min, queue p50 15.4 min, 90 inferred ejections for 151 merged PRs.

Instrumentation: nightly browser shards record V8 coverage with parsed-script observations retained across navigation; existing measurement artifacts contain completeness, exact tree, run and attempt plus per-case source identities. The planner verifies the full catalogue from successful exact-base nightly artifacts. Bounded fetches/scans and unobserved targets keep the full fallback; plan output records the fallback reason. This is dependency metadata, not reuse of test passes.

Correctness: focused tests cover the importing + non-importing navigation/HTML case (zero misses), Go/browser cap boundaries, new/unmapped/stale inputs, partial/failed/skipped/duplicate observations, scan bounds and symlinks. Recorded failure 37868981358 and all 80 historical change lists remain replayed. The attached selector-evidence.json compares 20 recent merged PRs (#425 through #410) before/after with zero omitted cases; all 20 already used full mode. Approved remote static validation on mbp2606 exits 0: 40 checks passed, zero optional skips. Nine focused selector/coverage regressions pass. Playwright native bootstrap/listing passes; one targeted runtime check was refused by another live host-wide browser lock, with no bypass.

Existing test expectations for unsafe narrowing now assert the entire gate. Consumer-reader selection assertions remain exercised on bounded dependency fixtures; no application assertion or test was removed, loosened or skipped. New selector tests run in the existing fixed go-static regression lane. All new source files are owned by audit slice S7 (scripts/**).

Follow-up owner: aeon-lead-claude (AEON-1014/AEON-1019 coordinator), to post the 7-day Delivery outcome on AEON-1019 after deployment: first-attempt green, inferred ejections, planner fallbacks/map completeness, and nightly coverage overhead. The coordinator owns cross-family review, PR publication and release gates.

Workflow handoff: OPS owns ci.yml. The tier planner and tier runners currently have contents-only permissions and no GH_TOKEN for nightly-artifact reads. OPS must expose the existing read authority before hosted map-based source narrowing can activate; until then the full browser fallback is the intended behavior. No new credential or PR-mode change is requested. The first complete nightly map is verified after the coordinator publishes this change.
